note.label: TO THE UNKNOWN GOD: ACTS 17

precepts.text: How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger! The beauty of Israel. So we were cast down to the earth, meaning we were brought down low, we were brought into captivity, we were not on top ruling any more. So this is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.
precepts.point: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations! When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. It is talking about a place of authority. When you read the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise. Then there is heaven which is the sky and space. And then there are heavens like a place of authority.

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground.” Who is Lucifer, and what heaven did he fall from? When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. In the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise; there is heaven that is the sky and space; and there are heavens that are a place of authority. Lamentations shows that last one.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” The beauty of Israel was cast down from heaven to the earth. That means we were brought down low: brought into captivity, no longer on top, no longer ruling. It is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.

So Lucifer falling from heaven is a ruler falling from his place of authority, not an angel falling out of the sky. Read on in Isaiah 14 and he is named: Israel will “take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city, because America is rich. And “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: Lucifer is a man, the man of sin, the fourth beast, the white man.

The same Lord who cast Israel down from heaven to the earth will cut this ruler down to the ground. It is a future prophecy of America being destroyed.

precepts.text: Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come. Remember we read in Isaiah 14, the king of Babylon. That great city Babylon, that mighty city. So their judgment comes in one hour.
precepts.point: Why does it say golden city? Because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. It is talking about a city, a country, rulers. It is talking about a government.

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.why:
“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” In the day the Lord gives us rest from our sorrow, our fear and the hard bondage we were made to serve in, we are going to be speaking against America. The king of Babylon here is America, and this is how we know Lucifer is not an angel: Lucifer is called the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city. In Revelation it is mystery Babylon the great, and Revelation 18 explains that city.

“Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” Remember what we read in Isaiah 14: the king of Babylon. Here it is that great city Babylon, that mighty city, and her judgment comes in one hour.

So Lucifer is a city, a country, rulers, a government. “The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.” It is not talking about a fallen angel; it is talking about America, the king of Babylon, whose ceasing Israel will proclaim when the Lord gives us rest from the hard bondage.

precepts.point: Why does it say golden city? Because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. It is talking about a city, a country, rulers. It is talking about a government.

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the king of Babylon “the golden city”: “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Why does it say golden city? Revelation 18 explains it: “For in one hour so great riches is come to nought.”

So great riches: that is the golden city. It is called golden because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. And all those riches come to nothing in one hour, the same hour of judgment in verse 10, when they stand afar off crying, “Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city!”

The golden city ceasing in Isaiah is the great riches coming to nought in Revelation. It is not an angel that falls; it is a rich nation, a government, the oppressor that made us serve in hard bondage, and in the day the Lord gives us rest, we will take up this proverb against it.

The rest Christ promises the labouring and heavy laden is rest from the sorrow, the fear and the hard bondage of Israel's captivity. The ones heavy laden are the people who were made to serve. That is who “come unto me” is addressed to.

Isaiah opens the chapter by saying who gets that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel.” We are messed up as a people, not in our right minds yet, but because of the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob he will yet choose us. That's mercy, and we need that mercy.

precepts.text: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel; the strangers shall be joined to the house of Jacob, and Israel shall rule over their oppressors. And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve. That is the true rest: after the Sabbath we go back to labouring in Esau's system Monday morning, but that day ends the bondage itself.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
The seventh day Sabbath, resting from our servile work, is a similitude the Most High uses for us resting in the kingdom when it is established. That is the true rest, when we will really rest from servile work. Because after the Sabbath some of us have to go to work on Sunday, then Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, slaving for Esau.

Isaiah shows the day of that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.” The nations are going to be joined with us, but how? “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” They are our possession.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” That is the true rest: rest from our sorrow, from our fear, and from the hard bondage we were made to serve.

That is why “if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.” That Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the Hamites, but we did not get true rest in the land; there were enemies on all sides, the Amalekites and the Hamites we were fighting. The true rest is the kingdom of God on earth, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.”

precepts.text: The Lord cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel: heaven is dominion and rulership, the high estate, and we were set down to a low state.
precepts.point: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man? Not, is this the fallen angel; not the Nephilim. Is this the man that made the earth to tremble? What man made the earth to tremble by dropping atom bombs everywhere? He's the man, the oppressor, the king of Babylon that we read about in this chapter. It is not going into some angel, because all the angels take their directive from the Most High God.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer”: before we can know who Lucifer is, we have to know what heaven is. Lamentations shows it: “How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.”

Heaven is dominion and rulership. That was the high standard, the high estate Israel held, and the beauty of Israel was cast down from it to the earth. We were set down to a low state. No one thinks Israel was literally thrown out of the sky; we fell from rulership.

So it is with Lucifer. Esau takes Jude and Isaiah 14, mixes them up and comes with this fallen angel teaching. But keep it in context. Lucifer, the lightbearer, is the king of Babylon of verse 4, the oppressor, the one who “smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke.” It is talking about a nation: this so-called white man, America, whom everybody looks at as god and all knowing because he controls communication everywhere.

He is falling from heaven the same way Israel did: he is losing his dominion and his rulership. “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”: not a fallen angel, not the Nephilim, but the man, the one who made the earth tremble by dropping atom bombs everywhere. The angels are not falling out of heaven; they take their directive from the Most High God.

precepts.text: The kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: that's rulership.
precepts.point: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man? Not, is this the fallen angel; not the Nephilim. Is this the man that made the earth to tremble? What man made the earth to tremble by dropping atom bombs everywhere? He's the man, the oppressor, the king of Babylon that we read about in this chapter. It is not going into some angel, because all the angels take their directive from the Most High God.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Daniel shows again what heaven means: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High.” That is rulership. The greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven is dominion over the nations, and it is given to the saints of the Most High, Israel.

So when Isaiah says “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!”, it is the fall of a ruler from his dominion. How did you fall from rulership? Lucifer is the king of Babylon, the oppressor who weakened the nations with his bombs, his lies and his fornication.

He said in his heart, “I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”, North America, and “I will be like the most High.” “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.”

Put the two together. The rulership he grasped at, he loses, and the kingdom and dominion under the whole heaven is given to the people of the saints of the Most High. It is not an angel cast out of the sky; it is the man, this so-called white man, America, brought down, and Israel lifted up to rule.

precepts.text: The devils cried out, Art thou come hither to torment us before the time? The demons recognized Christ, and they knew there is a time appointed of torment. So do not let any camp make you think you are going to escape judgment: there is a place appointed where evil spirits and evil people go to suffer torment. Some Israelite camps do counter classes saying there is no hell every time we teach it; they have no scripture to paint that picture.
precepts.point: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch: this is the future of the pride of America.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.why:
Isaiah says of the king of Babylon, “Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth”. Babylon is the United States of America, and hell is the destiny of its prideful rulers. Hell is a condition, and it is also a real place of torment and suffering. People say, you have nothing, you just walk around in purple clothes talking about the Bible. We know something you don't know: your ass is going to hell. Hell is a real place, and you're going there. We would not trade places with them for all the tea in China, for all the gold in Fort Knox.

Some Israelite camps teach there is no place of torment, and every time we teach about hell they make counter videos. So look at what the devils said to Christ. In the country of the Gergesenes “there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way.” “And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?”

The demons recognized Christ, and they knew there is a time appointed for torment. Then “the devils besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine.” An evil spirit needs a vessel to inhabit. “And he said unto them, Go.” The whole herd “ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters.” The Lord has a place where evil spirits go to suffer torment.

There is a time appointed when everybody who is evil, Israelite or not, is going to pay. Do not let any camp make you think you will escape judgment; they have no scripture to paint that picture.

Why would God make such a place? Because there are people on this earth who do not care about death, prison or you; they will do the most depraved things and laugh about it on the way to the grave. There has to be an extreme punishment for people who disregard life. If there were no hell and no place of suffering, God would not be feared. So there is a hell, God has it prepared, and the wicked, including wicked Israelites, are going into it.

precepts.text: Why did Paul open with, Hath God cast away his people? Because of the northern and southern kingdom conflict: the Jews thought God was not dealing with the northern kingdom. I would not that ye should be ignorant of this mystery: blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in; God blinded a portion so the gospel could be preached to the northern kingdom living as Gentiles. And so all Israel shall be saved means both kingdoms, all twelve tribes, can be saved. It is not a license saying the wicked escape hell; that is not what Paul was talking about.
precepts.point: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch: this is the future of the pride of America.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.why:
Some Israelite camps use “all Israel shall be saved” to argue that even the wicked will escape hell. To see what Paul meant, start from the beginning of the chapter: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.”

Why did Paul open that way? Because of the conflict between the northern and southern kingdoms. The Jews thought God was not dealing with the northern kingdom anymore, since God had told them, you are not my people, and Hosea said that where it was said unto them, you are not my people, there they would be called the children of the living God. Paul, of Benjamin, was of the southern kingdom, and he answers, “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.”

“For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.” The mystery is that God is dealing with both the northern and southern kingdoms, which is why the chapter talks about them being grafted back in. God blinded a portion, the Jews, to salvation in Jesus Christ so that the gospel could be preached to the northern kingdom living as Gentiles, so they could come in. If you say you're an Israelite and you still don't understand this chapter after all these years, you're an idiot, and God is not dealing with you.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. That means both kingdoms, all twelve tribes, can be saved. It is not a license saying a murderer, an adulterer or a thief will be saved at the end no matter what. You see how stupid they are? Leaders who use this verse to say you are not going to hell are wise in their own conceits. There is a hell, and if you go against God you are going into it, Israelite or not.

precepts.text: Isaac told Esau, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and by thy sword shalt thou live. That is why they do not want anybody else to have a weapon: a nuclear weapon is a sword, and they rule because they have the ability to kill and destroy anything that comes against them. That is why the Pope calling for peace is called weak.
precepts.point: But thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch: this is the future of the pride of America.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.why:
Isaiah describes the king of Babylon as “He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke, he that ruled the nations in anger”. That is how they got where they are: they took this land with bloodshed, massacred the indigenous people, dragged Negroes to America against their will for hundreds of years and used us for free labor, and they are still always looking for a reason to start a war.

Isaac told Esau where that comes from: “Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;” “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.”

Esau was given the fatness of the earth, and he lives by the sword. That is why they do not want anybody else to have a weapon. A nuclear weapon is a sword, and they rule because they can kill and destroy anything that comes against them. It is why they go to war with Iran over nuclear capability they have been talking about for thirty years, even when their own officials ask why.

It is also why the Pope calling for peace gets called weak. For a people who live by the sword, peace looks like weakness. But the same chapter of Isaiah says the one who weakened the nations will be cut down to the ground, because the pride of his heart has deceived him.

precepts.text: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and yet choose Israel and set them in their own land: God, not the League of Nations or the UN.
precepts.point: For this same purpose have I raised thee up: Paul could not condemn Rome aloud so he compared Esau to Pharaoh. God raised Pharaoh, Rome and now America, the extension of Rome, to show his power; no other nation takes America down, so he lets her have every advance and then flexes.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
“As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” Some say the Hebrew means loved less; that is such malarkey. “Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid. For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy”. God is not unrighteous for choosing Jacob.

“So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.” You cannot will yourself to be the people of God, and you cannot run around setting up churches to be the people of God. It is of God that showeth mercy.

And Isaiah says who God will show that mercy to: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. That is what God said he is going to do. Not the League of Nations, not the UN, not America: God.

So the Zionists who set themselves up in the land by the nations have not been set there by God. Jacob, whom God loved, is the one he will have mercy on and choose again and set in their own land, and Esau, whom he hated, is raised up like Pharaoh only so that God can show his power in bringing him down.

precepts.text: I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: space travel. I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north: that is us, in North America. I will ascend above the heights of the clouds: airplanes. How could that part be true, because you see it, but the verse above it about the stars be fake?
precepts.point: Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and stablisheth a city by iniquity. America was built with blood: the schools, the churches, and the courthouses are on the bones and blood of our brothers and sisters. Did not Cain establish a city by iniquity? There is no new thing under the sun.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

precepts.why:
Habakkuk says, “Woe to him that coveteth an evil covetousness to his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the power of evil!” Is that not what Nimrod and them were doing? Before we get scattered, let us build a tower and get up to heaven. Today's Babylon has the same characteristics and attributes. Jeremiah said it too: “Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from me shall spoilers come unto her”.

Isaiah shows the heart of it: “For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”. That is space travel. NASA and SpaceX are advancing plans for a permanent presence on the moon through the Artemis program, and Artemis 2 just went up. Elon Musk talks of colonizing Mars. Why does Esau the Edomite want to go to Mars? Because it is the red planet.

“I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: that is us, in North America. “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: that is airplanes. How could that part be true, because you see it, while the verse above it about the stars is fake? You can have your doubting Thomas saying it's all fake. Is it fake like the planes you fly on and the helicopters you see? Stop watching stupid YouTube clips.

He sets his nest on high thinking he will be delivered from the power of evil when destruction comes. But he “hast consulted shame to thy house by cutting off many people”. “Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and stablisheth a city by iniquity!” America was built with blood: the schools, the churches and the courthouses are on the bones and blood of our brothers and sisters. Did not Cain establish a city by iniquity? There is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.text: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, choose Israel, and set them in their own land, and the strangers shall be joined with them and cleave to the house of Jacob. The people shall bring them to their place: the Arabs out of North Africa, which is Ham's, the white man out of Australia and South Africa. Israel shall possess them for servants and handmaids, take them captives whose captives they were, and rule over their oppressors, and the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow and from the hard bondage. Come unto me all ye that labour is rest from slavery and oppression, not just from sin.
precepts.point: The glory of Lebanon, the fir, pine, and box, shall beautify the place of my sanctuary; Lebanon and its famous trees belong to the Israelites. The sons of them that afflicted thee shall come bending, and all that despised thee shall bow at the soles of thy feet and call thee the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. That is what Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not under Edom.

note.label: Prophesy From Pain to Peace

precepts.why:
What about the strangers? Are they going to be in the kingdom? Yes, but read how. “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody on the planet. He said Jacob: the twelve tribes of Israel. That's us. He will set them in their own land: not the League of Nations, not the UN.

Then: “and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: joined to obey us. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”. All nations will be put where they rightfully belong. The Arabs in North Africa are not supposed to be there; that belongs to Ham, and they will be moved out. The white man in Australia does not belong there, and the white man in South Africa will be removed out of that land.

Then: “and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors”. That is the law of Leviticus 25 just read: the laws will be re-implemented.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”. That is why Christ said come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. People say rest from sin; not just sin. Slavery is the result of sin, and oppression is the result of sin. That is the rest Christ was talking about.

Back in Isaiah 60, that is why “the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: we will possess them, as servants and handmaids. The Bible does not contradict itself; Christianity contradicts the Bible.

precepts.text: Upon her forehead was a name written, Mystery Babylon the Great, the mother of harlots. It is similitude, not a literal brothel. Everybody but our own people can see this is the United States of America, not Iraq. John, who lived under Rome, was not writing about ancient Babylon.
precepts.point: God is hardening the hearts of the neocons and Donald Trump's circle to do exactly what he wants, as he did with Pharaoh. AIPAC funds both parties and Candace Owens and Tucker Carlson see it but cannot stop it. How could a country not even as big as Jordan control the world's largest military? Because God is a master and the least of the flock had to draw them out.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon.” We know from Psalms 137 that the United States of America is the daughter of Babylon, and Isaiah is speaking prophetically of Babylon the Great to come, the same one John wrote about in Revelation.

“And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS.” Is that saying Babylon is one big brothel, with the main hoe in the United States pimping out the other hoes? No. It is similitude.

Think about who wrote it. John lived way after Isaiah, during the Roman Empire, long after ancient Babylon had fallen. Why would John be writing about ancient Babylon? He is talking about the same Babylon the Great Isaiah saw: the United States of America. This is not talking about Iraq.

Everybody sees it except the Israelites. They will say no one knows who this is. Are you kidding me? Our Black people, our Hispanics and Native Americans who cannot see it, we hope the Lord opens your eyes.

That is why Isaiah asks, “Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms; That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof?” The man is the so-called white man running the United States, whose real power began with the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in '45. He is weakening the nations, even his own allies like India and Japan, which depend on oil coming through the Strait of Hormuz, and God is hardening the hearts of Trump's circle to do just what he wants, as he did with Egypt.

precepts.text: Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them? The fourth beast overcame all with much wicked oppression over the whole compass of the earth.
precepts.point: Iran has not forgotten what America did and God has not forgotten what America is doing in the earth. America will have its demise.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” This is what Lucifer does, what the beast does. Iran has not forgotten what America did, and God has not forgotten what America is doing in the earth right now and all the evil it has done before. The Lord is saying America will have its demise, because of all the evil it is doing on the earth.

“Which didst weaken the nations”: they have Cuba on its knees right now, and those are our brothers and sisters over there. Trump threatened tariffs on any country that sells oil to Cuba, said there will be no more oil or money going to Cuba, zero, and put pressure on Mexico until Mexico pulled away. Then he says Cuba looks ready to fall. Why is it ready to fall? Because you are causing it, Trump. It is the same thing they did to Iran, and to Venezuela. This is what they do everywhere they go.

Ezra names that beast: “Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?” Esau is the fourth beast, and he is going to bring the end of the times; you can see why.

“And the fourth came, and overcame all the beasts that were past, and had power over the world with great fearfulness, and over the whole compass of the earth with much wicked oppression.” Power over the whole compass of the earth, with much wicked oppression: that is America weakening the nations, and that is why it will be cut down to the ground.

precepts.text: Hell from beneath is moved for thee, it stirreth up the dead, all the chief ones of the earth and the kings of the nations, and they say, Art thou also become weak as we? How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning, cut down to the ground. The nations rising up to destroy this place.
precepts.point: The heaven shall reveal his iniquity: as we teach, the angels make things happen until the whole world sees America and Israel as the oppressor. And the earth shall rise up against him.

note.label: Cyber Warfare: The Mouth Of The Beast

precepts.why:
Job 20 is talking about America being destroyed: “a fire not blown shall consume him”, the nuclear bomb that needs no fanning to burn; “it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle”, left here in America. “The heaven shall reveal his iniquity”: as we teach the word of God, the angels make things happen, Europe starts showing America's shame, and everybody sees America, and Israel too, as the oppressor. Europe has already brought charges against Netanyahu and put out a warrant for his arrest for war crimes. “and the earth shall rise up against him.”

Who is the earth that shall rise up against him? The nations. Isaiah explains it: “Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, even all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.” Hell is the low condition everybody on earth is in under him. Raised up from their thrones: all the nations rising up to fight against America and destroy America.

“All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?”

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” How are you fallen from ruling, O America. That is the earth rising up against him: the nations he weakened rising up to destroy this place.

precepts.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers.
precepts.point: They intended evil and imagined a mischievous device which they are not able to perform.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the Lord shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them.” That sounds just like Malachi 4: “the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven”, and “it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Nuclear fire is coming to America. And David goes on: “Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.” Neither root nor branch: their children will be cut off too.

Isaiah shows why the children are cut off: “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers.” For the sins of their forefathers. The forefathers committed the crime, got the bag from us, took the wealth, took everything from us, and now the children are left holding the bag. Esau, and not just Esau: Elam, Ishmael, the Hamites. All of them got wealthy off the backs of the Israelites; all of them had us in slavery one way or another.

It is done “that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew.” Son and nephew goes right back to Psalm 21 and the end of Malachi 4: their seed destroyed from among the children of men.

Why? “For they intended evil against thee: they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” They imagine evil devices and evil counsels against us, but “He disappointeth the devices of the crafty”, and “he saveth the poor from the sword.” The poor are Israel: “the poor of his people shall trust in it.” So the fiery oven is for the nations that enslaved us, down to their children, and the Lord saves his poor from their sword.

precepts.text: The Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.
precepts.point: He saveth the poor from the sword. The poor are Israel.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. He taketh the wise in their own craftiness”. The crafty are the nations, in particular Esau, that counsel against us and keep exploiting, oppressing and colonizing with imperialism. It is the same as Psalms 21: “they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” Their counsel is carried headlong; they are going to fall headlong and bust their forehead. “They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.”

“But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” From Esau's sword, the nations' sword. Who is the poor? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

Write it down, brothers: when the scripture talks about the poor, it is talking about Israel, the poor of his people who trust in Zion. That was an easy one, and every soldier should know it.

And before the Lord saves the poor from the sword, the wicked has to be identified. The man of sin must be revealed, so that the whole earth knows who he is: the nation that bombed country after country, removed leader after leader, and made the earth to tremble.

precepts.text: I will break the Assyrian in my land; then shall his yoke depart from off them.
precepts.point: The coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah, and the Lord will turn away their captivity.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
Jeremiah's word came “against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.” The Philistines are the Palestinians. Some scriptures are twofold, threefold, fourfold: Pharaoh smote Gaza then, and today Netanyahu and the Israelis, Amalek, smite Gaza.

Isaiah shows what happens to the one smiting: “That I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot”. The Assyrian here is Amalek, and Amalek will be judged. “then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders”: Amalek's yoke departs from off the Palestinians. “This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth: and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations.” All nations are going to get judgment.

But jump to verse 29: “Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken”. Palestinians, do not rejoice because Amalek is moved out of the way. “for out of the serpent’s root shall come forth a cockatrice, and his fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent”: a missile. “And the firstborn of the poor shall feed”, and the firstborn of the poor is Christ; “and I will kill thy root with famine, and he shall slay thy remnant.”

“Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou, whole Palestina, art dissolved: for there shall come from the north a smoke”. Palestine will be dissolved. Not only Amalek, but the Palestinians have to get out of that land too. “the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

precepts.text: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
precepts.point: When he falls, the whole earth is at rest and breaks forth into singing.

note.label: War of the Gods

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Lucifer is another name for Esau, alongside Tyrus and Edom, and further up the chapter he is called the king of Babylon. How did he weaken the nations? Through war. A US destroyer took down two fighter jets in ninety-three seconds, having calculated seventeen ways to kill them before they reached altitude. Venezuela’s defenses, its bases and its president were taken in thirty minutes. That is why his pride is lifted up, and why the ignorant say he must be God.

Isaiah 13 names what he is: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms.” The Space Command headquarters moving to Huntsville, Alabama, now to be called Rocket City, means more weaponry, the smith and the waster that God created. Babylon is the glory of kingdoms: all these nations want to come to Babylon and get a piece of it. They call it the American dream.

The world is amazed at the beast: “Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?” But that same verse of Isaiah 13 says the glory of kingdoms shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. The Lord “hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers. He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”, primarily God’s people, is brought down.

So the glory of kingdoms falls from heaven like Lucifer, and then “The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet: they break forth into singing.” When these devils fall, the whole earth will finally be at rest.

precepts.text: The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.
precepts.point: The Lord will bring Israel up out of the land of the north, North America.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God.” That is America going into space; America was the first there, and America invented the airplane that ascends “above the heights of the clouds.” “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north.” That is the Monroe Doctrine, now the Donroe Doctrine. The congregation is Mexico, Central and South America, Panama, Puerto Rico, Dominica, Jamaica, Trinidad and the Caribbean islands, where the twelve tribes of Israel are. America, the king of Babylon, the oppressor, sits upon the congregation and rules over us: fall in line, or what we did to Maduro we will do to you. And it is in the sides of the north, North America; that is why its treaty with Europe is called the North Atlantic Treaty.

Jeremiah shows where Israel is: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt; But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north.” The land of the north is North America. It is going to be said that the Lord brought the children of Israel out of this side of the world.

“and from all the lands whither he had driven them: and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” Israel is in North America and all through this hemisphere, and 2 Esdras speaks of the ten tribes coming to this side of the world.

So the one who sits on the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north is sitting on Israel. According to prophecy, America will be sitting on these congregations in the last days, during the fourth seal, and bad things are about to happen on this side of the world. But the Lord will bring his people up out of the land of the north.

precepts.text: Lucifer, cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations.
precepts.point: Esau is the same people from the youngest to the oldest.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
The Lord hated Esau and calls his people “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Isaiah shows what that people does in the earth: “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Esau weakens the nations.

How? Economic, political and military power. Look at what Donald Trump is doing in Venezuela and in Africa right now. They bombed Nigeria on Christmas Day and claimed it was to protect Christians from persecution. They bombed Venezuela and claimed it was to stop drug trafficking, while Mexico, on America's own border, has more drug cartels than any place in the world. They want the oil. Later Trump said it plainly, return the oil to our land, as if Venezuela ever stole oil or land from America. The rich think the poor are stupid and will believe anything, and our people believe it.

And America always puts a black face on it. Before they attacked Iraq it was Colin Powell, lying about weapons of mass destruction. Before they bombed a black nation for its oil, they did not pick a lawyer, a doctor or an engineer. They picked a hoe, the same black woman who was shaking her behind, reading what they told her to read about defending Christians in Nigeria. That is the ultimate disrespect to black people.

The hypocrisy is plain. In Jerusalem the so-called Jews say they spit on the ground when they see a crucifix, call for killing Christians, and spit in a Christian woman's face in the street, and nobody bombs them to defend Christians. There is no truth in the white man. If he says look up, you better look down.

Micah shows the same people: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand. And they covet fields, and take them by violence.” The oil in Nigeria and Venezuela, the diamonds and the copper in Africa. America was built by violence on stolen land. That is Lucifer weakening the nations, and why God says, “Never trust thine enemy.”

precepts.text: God created the smith who brings forth the weapon and the waster to destroy.
precepts.point: Once Esau falls, he will never rise again.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
“Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.” “For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew.” To cut them off means he is going to kill all of them. When Esau falls, Esau will never rise back again.

Some think Esau will never fall. You forgot what happened to the Babylonians, the Persians and Medes, the Greeks, Rome and Egypt, all superpowers in their time. America has bombs, lasers, all types of weapons, the most powerful military on the planet. But the Most High is more powerful than America.

Isaiah shows how he does it: “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” The smith today is what you call the scientist who makes weapons. Back then they were called smiths; they bring forth the instrument for the work. And the waster is nuclear power. God let them create the waster, and it is made to destroy.

Job shows it striking the wicked: “He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.” The iron weapon is the missile.

So the slaughter prepared for Esau’s children is by the very weapons God allowed their own smiths to make. Nobody is innocent, and whatever evil was done to the Israelites, no one is getting away with it.

precepts.text: Gather yourselves together, O nation not desired, before the decree bring forth.
precepts.point: The nations shall bring Israel to its place and serve as servants and handmaids.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Before he sets us in our land, he tells the twelve tribes what to do: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” We are the nation not desired, and God is instructing the twelve tribes to gather themselves together, to wake up.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.” That decree is the destruction that is prophesied to come. Get yourselves together before destruction comes. Things are moving at a quicker pace, and that is why the Bishop says he loves President Trump: he is forcing prophecies to come to pass and forcing the Israelites to do what the Bible says.

Who gathers? “Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” The meek are humble to God’s word, men and women who do his commandments without making excuses. We cannot gather with camps that say we are not keeping any Sabbath, or that throw you out for wearing fringes with a border of blue.

Then the judgment on the land: “For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation.” “I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant.” The Palestinians are not just pushed out; according to the Bible they are destroyed. “And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah”, “for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.” That is Israel set in their own land.

precepts.text: Can two walk together except they be agreed?
precepts.point: The nations shall bring Israel to its place and serve as servants and handmaids.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Gather yourselves together” does not mean gather with everybody. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?”

You get some morons that say, Let’s join ourselves with the camp that believes John the Baptist was a wicked nigger. You cannot join with that. Let’s join with the camp that believes men do not have to work: get seven women, eight women, and let them work for you. No, we cannot join with that.

Some people are simple, and they ask, Why aren’t y’all all together? This is why. Two cannot walk together unless they are agreed, and the ones who gather are those who “have wrought his judgment”, the meek who do God’s laws, seek righteousness and seek meekness.

So when the Lord will yet choose Israel and set them in their own land, the gathering before the decree is not one of mixed doctrines. It is a gathering of those agreed on God’s commandments.

precepts.text: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.
precepts.point: The nations shall bring Israel to its place and serve as servants and handmaids.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
The Lord “will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Judah shall live on the sea coast, and it gets better: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” And Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” The tabernacle of David is the twelve tribes, built again as in the days of old.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.” There are people calling themselves Jewish today, and Jew comes from Judah, praise of Yahawah; they are not the praise of Yahawah. And people calling themselves Christians, the anointed ones; they are not the anointed ones.

“And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them.” There are waste cities all over there, and after Armageddon there will be more. And we will have servants: that is the strangers joined to the house of Jacob, the heathen round about us as bondmen and bondmaids, when that law goes back in full effect.

“And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God.” That is Isaiah 14:1 fulfilled: set in their own land, never pulled out again.

precepts.text: The Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.
precepts.point: Israel shall be named priests of the Lord, receive double for its shame, and its seed shall be known among the Gentiles.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek.” Christ read it in Luke 4 as “to preach the gospel to the poor.” When it says the poor, who is that? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

That is telling you who the poor are: the poor of Zion, the poor of his people. Zion is another name for the Israelites.

And Isaiah 61 itself agrees: he came “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes”. Why are we mourning? Because we are captive.

So the good tidings, the brokenhearted, the captives and them that are bound are not all nations. They are the poor of the Lord’s people, the Israelites in captivity, who shall trust in the Zion the Lord has founded.

precepts.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers. That is not what we said; that is what God said.
precepts.point: If the reproach falls on the descendants, they are direct beneficiaries of the evil their forefathers did. That is fact.

precepts.point: The word gospel means good news. It's good news to a slave to hear that they have redemption coming, good news to a servant to hear that they have a great day of deliverance coming.

precepts.point: The vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: Esau. Fitted to destruction means created to be destroyed.

precepts.point: You might forget all that happened to your ancestors, but God never forgets.

precepts.point: Thy pomp is brought down to the grave: pomp means pride. The noise of thy viols is their music system, their church system.

precepts.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; the name and remnant are cut off, so none escape by saying it was only the forefathers.
precepts.point: The enmity was set from the garden between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed. They bruised Christ's heel, but at the end of the world Jacob bruises the head: the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

precepts.why:
War with Amalek from generation to generation means the children answer for the fathers. “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities. For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew, saith the Lord.”

The name, the remnant, the son and the nephew are cut off, so none escape by saying it was only the forefathers. Forty years after Rephidim the children of Amalek had done nothing themselves and were still marked; hundreds of years later Saul was sent against their seed. The nations do not get away with what they did to His people, and the judgment carries to the seed until the remembrance is put out from under heaven.

precepts.text: The Lord founded Zion, and the poor of His people shall trust in it, identifying the poor as His chosen.
precepts.point: The poor of the Bible is the poor of His people, those that keep His laws, statutes, and commandments. So the poor have hope, and iniquity stops her mouth.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why:
“But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” Who is the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of the Bible is the poor of his people, those that keep his laws, statutes, and commandments, his chosen. The crafty meet with darkness in the daytime and grope in the noonday as in the night, walking in sin and darkness, but even though the heathen rage and their wrath comes at us to kill us, the Lord saves the poor. So the poor have hope, and iniquity stops her mouth.

precepts.text: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and choose Israel, and they shall rule over their oppressors and take captive those whose captives they were.
precepts.point: The Lord hears the desire of the humble and prepares their heart, causing his ear to hear, so as to judge the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may oppress no more. The Israelites will not be oppressed anymore.

note.label: Psalm 10: Why Standest Thou Afar Off, O Lord

precepts.why:
“Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man: seek out his wickedness till thou find none. The Lord is King for ever and ever: the heathen are perished out of his land.” The so-called white man and the other nations must be put down so the Lord can flourish, because Christ shares no throne with the other nations; America is not moving out of the way for Christ's kingdom. The so-called jewish, whom the bible calls bastards dwelling in Ashdod, the Lord will root out of his land.

Isaiah shows the day: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob. And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and choose Israel, and they shall take captive those whose captives they were and rule over their oppressors.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”. That is the Lord hearing the desire of the humble and judging the fatherless and the oppressed, that the man of the earth may oppress no more. The Israelites will not be oppressed anymore.

precepts.text: The Lord has founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it. Zion is the Israelites, so the poor the Lord speaks of are the Israelites.
precepts.point: Blessed is he that considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble. This applies to the whole nation, because we are the poor.

note.label: Psalm 41: Blessed Is He That Considers the Poor

precepts.why:
“Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the Lord will deliver him in time of trouble.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” Zion is the Israelites, so the poor the Lord speaks of are the Israelites.

That is why this applies to the whole nation: we are the poor. The one who considers the poor, the Lord will preserve and keep alive, bless upon the earth, and not deliver “unto the will of his enemies.”

precepts.text: He said in his heart he would ascend into heaven, exalt his throne above the stars of God, and sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”. This is the boasting of the mighty man. He said in his heart he would ascend into heaven, exalt his throne above the stars of God, and sit upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the north.

The congregation is the congregation of the Lord, Israel, and the north is where he rules over them. Esau boasts that he will sit over the Most High's congregation. That is the pride of heart that deceived him, and the man of sin has to be revealed for who he is.

precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High.” That is the boast of the mighty man in his mischief: he will be like the most High. This is why Esau paints Christ white and makes himself the image of God; he said in his heart he would be like the most High. Our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, but here is his own boast, and the pride of his heart has deceived him.

precepts.text: Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.” The one who said in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground, who boasted he would ascend into heaven and be like the most High, is brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit. The mighty man boasting himself in mischief ends there. The pride of his heart deceived him, and the Most High brings him down.

precepts.text: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble; Satan is a man, Lucifer is a man.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”. Is this the man. Satan is a man; Lucifer is a man. The mighty man of Psalm 52 who boasts himself in mischief is looked upon narrowly when he is brought down, and the ones who see him ask, is this the man that made the earth to tremble and shook kingdoms?

That is the man of sin revealed. Our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ, but the scriptures call him a man.

precepts.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer; the man of sin is revealed as a man, not a horned figure with a pitchfork.
precepts.point: The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Lucifer, who said he would ascend into heaven and be like the most High, is fallen and cut down to the ground. He weakened the nations.

The man of sin is revealed as a man, not a horned figure with a pitchfork. The white picture of Jesus is a deception, and the devil is Esau, the boasting mighty man who dwells in the clefts of the rock and rules over the congregation in the north. The Bible says nothing of a horned devil; it says, is this the man.

precepts.text: They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble; the righteous will marvel that he is brought to nothing.
precepts.point: The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him”. Isaiah shows what they see: “They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”. The righteous will look narrowly on the boasting mighty man when he is brought down and marvel that he is brought to nothing. Is this the man that made the earth to tremble? That is why they laugh at him.

precepts.text: The poor of His people is the people of Zion, the Israelites, who shall trust in what the Most High has founded.
precepts.point: He shall break in pieces the oppressor, which is why this is pointing to things to come, the Kingdom of Heaven.

note.label: Psalm 72: All Nations Shall Serve Him

precepts.why:
David asks the Most High to give the king his judgments and the king's son his righteousness, so that “He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment.” Who is the poor? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people is the people of Zion, the Israelites, who shall trust in what the Most High has founded. So when the king's son judges the poor with judgment and “shall save the children of the needy”, it is the Israelites being judged rightly and saved.

“The mountains shall bring peace to the people, and the little hills, by righteousness”, and he “shall break in pieces the oppressor.” That is why this is pointing to things to come, the Kingdom of Heaven, when the poor of Zion are saved and their oppressor is broken.

precepts.text: What shall one answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of His people, the Israelites, shall trust in it.
precepts.point: Let this be the reward of my adversaries from the Lord, and of them that speak evil against my soul. The adversaries are the nations, and the Lord fights for us against our enemies to save us.

note.label: Psalm 109: Give Myself unto Prayer

precepts.why:
“Because that he remembered not to shew mercy, but persecuted the poor and needy man”. The poor and needy man is Israel. “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people, the Israelites, trust in Zion which the Lord has founded. The enemies showed us no mercy in captivity and continued to destroy us even when our iniquity came to an end; that is the answer to the messengers of the nation.

precepts.text: The house of Israel shall possess the nations for servants and handmaids in the land of the Lord.
precepts.point: The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for.

note.label: Jeremiah 48: The Prophecy Against Moab

precepts.why:
The Lord knows Moab's wrath, “but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.” Isaiah shows how it ends for the proud nations: “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”

The house of Israel shall possess the nations for servants and handmaids in the land of the Lord. Moab, that enslaved us and built whole industries off our people, will be brought to his place and possessed by the children of God he oppressed; they shall take them captives whose captives they were, and rule over their oppressors.

precepts.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, the cry of astonishment over the downfall of the proud, renowned power, matched again in the judgment of Tyrus.
precepts.point: They shall take up a lamentation, asking how she is destroyed, that renowned city inhabited of seafaring men which was strong in the sea and caused terror on all who haunted it. This parallels the fall of the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today.

note.label: Ezekiel 26: The Fall of Tyrus

precepts.why:
The princes of the sea cry, “How art thou destroyed”, astonished that the renowned city which caused terror on all that haunt it could fall. Isaiah records that same cry over Lucifer: “How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!”

It is the cry of astonishment over the downfall of the proud, renowned power, the one who weakened the nations, and it is matched again in the judgment of Tyrus. She who was strong in the sea and made the isles shake is cut down, and the princes lay away their robes and tremble at every moment.

That is what waits for the great seafaring city that reflects Esau's nation today: the same fall, the same astonishment.

precepts.text: They shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.
precepts.point: Behold, I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me. Israel does not have to lift a finger.

note.label: Zechariah 2: The Measuring Line and the Apple of His Eye
